verdicts.rewritten_summary: Official gazette text of State Law 4/2023 of 28 February 2023 (BOE no. 51, 1 March 2023), the law for the real and effective equality of trans people and the guarantee of LGBTI rights: Title II allows adults to rectify the registered sex marker by simple declaration, with no requirement of prior medical diagnosis or treatment, and provides for corresponding document adaptation. The law further mandates public-policy, workplace, health and education measures, and its transitory provisions govern rectification applications pending at entry into force. Implementation of the administrative and education-facing provisions falls to the autonomous communities, this region's government among them.

verdicts.rewritten_summary: Human Rights Watch, 16 February 2023, on the Spanish Congress of Deputies' passage of the trans-equality law: legal gender recognition by self-identification through a simple administrative process, replacing the previous requirements of a gender-dysphoria diagnosis and two years of medical treatment. The law also expands access to assisted reproduction, strengthens sexuality education, bans medically unnecessary normalising surgery on intersex children before consent, enables parental recognition for unmarried same-sex couples, and prohibits LGBTI discrimination in healthcare, employment and housing; children from age 12 can obtain recognition under conditions, a provision that sparked political conflict. HRW places the reform within European and international standards against abusive, disproportionate requirements for legal gender recognition.
verdicts.note: rule-5 keep: record claims the 2023 registry reform drew an international rights organisation's autonomy-first ranking of the country; HRW report supports that claim; no region-specific source covers it
